newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL short-term rates ease due to fall in overnight.
newsitem.headline: KL short-term rates ease due to fall in overnight.

text.p: Short-term interbank rates eased after the fall in the overnight rate on Monday, which indicated availablity of ample liquidity in the system, dealers said on Tuesday.
They said the one-week interbank rate fell to 7.00/20 percent against 7.40/50, two-week declined to 7.10/20 against 7.40/60 and one-month was at 7.20/25 against 7.20/30.
Three-month interbank rate was quoted at 7.25/30 percent against 7.28/33 and six-month at 7.28/32 against 7.30/35.
"This fall in rates is mainly due to the fall in overnight on Monday. That showed the market there was money around," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
The overnight rate slipped to 6.0 percent on Monday against 8.0 percent on Friday as liquidity improved due to the maturity of a Bank Negara deposit.
Dealers said term rates should have fallen on Monday, but the market was cautious after a 500 million ringgit Bank Negara bill maturity on Friday failed to move interest rates.
"Once banks realised that there was excess liquidity in the afternoon, the overnight was pushed down," one dealer said.
In Malaysia, term money is traded in the morning and overnight money in the afternoon.
However, the interest rates were unlikely to fall any further as the funds availability was not very large, the dealers said.
